title: Advanced Prefetch Patterns
description: Explore advanced prefetching patterns including visibility-based prefetching, router integration, and lifecycle coordination.

data.text: Advanced prefetching goes beyond hover and route changes. By combining visibility APIs, router hooks, and lifecycle events, you can build a data-fetching system that feels telepathic. This lesson covers patterns for prefetching on mount, visibility changes, and coordinated background refetching.

Prefetching on mount is useful when a page or component always needs specific data. Instead of waiting for the first render to trigger a query, you prefetch during the initial load. This is especially powerful in Server Components where you can prefetch before the client ever hydrates.

data.title: Prefetch on Mount
data.content: Prefetching dashboard data when the component mounts

data.title: Server-First Mount Prefetching
data.text: In Next.js App Router, prefetch on mount is better done in the Server Component using prefetchQuery. The client-side mount prefetch is a fallback for Client Components that need the same treatment.

The Page Visibility API tells you when a tab is visible or hidden. You can use this to prefetch data when the user switches back to your app, ensuring that data they likely need is fresh. Combined with staleTime, this creates a seamless background refresh experience.

data.title: Visibility-Based Prefetch
data.content: Prefetching feed data when the tab becomes visible

data.text: Most modern routers expose navigation events or link hover events. By tapping into these events, you can prefetch data for the target route before the user completes navigation. This is especially effective in Next.js where next/link can be augmented with prefetch logic.

data.title: Router Prefetch Pattern
data.content: Prefetching on route hover with Next.js Link

data.text: Prefetching works best when paired with background refetching. When a user returns to a tab or navigates back, React Query can refetch stale data in the background. By tuning staleTime and gcTime, you control when prefetched data is considered fresh versus when it should be silently refreshed.

data.title: Network Saturation
data.text: Aggressive prefetching can saturate the network, especially on slow connections. Always respect the browser's HTTP/2 connection limits and consider using the Network Information API to reduce prefetching on slow networks.

Search interfaces benefit enormously from prefetching. As the user types or selects filters, you can prefetch results for likely next inputs. This turns a sequential search experience into an almost instant one.

terms.definition: Browser API that exposes whether the current tab is visible or hidden, enabling context-aware data loading.
A limit on concurrent prefetch requests to prevent network saturation. Typically 2-3 simultaneous fetches.
Duration after which data is considered stale and eligible for background refetching.

data.title: Build a Prefetch-Aware Navigation System
data.description: Implement a navigation sidebar where hovering over any link prefetches that page's data. Include a prefetch budget of 2 concurrent requests.
steps: Create a NavLink component that accepts a queryKey and queryFn
Implement a simple prefetch queue that limits concurrent prefetches to 2
Add a visual indicator showing which links have been prefetched
Verify in DevTools that only 2 requests are in flight at any time
data.expectedOutcome: Hovering nav links prefetches data with a concurrency limit. Navigation feels instant.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Prefetch on mount for always-needed data
Router hover events signal user intent
Limit concurrent prefetches with a budget
Search prefetching turns latency into immediacy
data.takeaway: Advanced prefetching patterns create a proactive data layer that anticipates user needs.
